_note: Method/judgment skill: the output is a disciplined investigation, not an exact string. Mostly qualitative. Under test: it investigates the root cause before changing code, tests one variable at a time, writes a failing repro test before fixing, and escalates after repeated failed fixes.

evals.name: root-cause-before-fix
evals.prompt: The login endpoint returns 500 intermittently. Just try a few things to make it stop.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT start guess-and-check. Should first reproduce consistently, read the error/stack trace, check recent changes, and trace the data flow backward — then form a hypothesis. Resists 'try a few things'.

assertions.text: investigates root cause (reproduce, read trace, check recent changes) before changing any code
does not apply multiple speculative changes at once

evals.name: single-variable-hypothesis
evals.prompt: I think it's either the cache, the DB pool, or the retry logic. Change all three and see.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to change all three at once. Should pick one hypothesis, make a single-variable change, verify, and only then move to the next — so the cause is actually identifiable.

assertions.text: tests one hypothesis / one variable at a time rather than changing all three together

evals.name: failing-test-first-then-escalate
evals.prompt: Root cause found: off-by-one in the pagination offset. Fix it. (Note: three earlier fixes already failed.)
evals.expected_output: Should write a failing test that reproduces the off-by-one first, then the minimal fix, then verify the suite. Given three earlier fixes failed, should also raise whether the architecture/assumption is wrong rather than just patching again.

assertions.text: writes a failing repro test before implementing the fix
